anti_patterns: Routing through Protect while also gossiping the same signed transaction to the public mempool: the public copy is sandwichable and nullifies the private path
Treating builder privacy as consensus-grade: assuming inclusion, censorship-resistance, or post-inclusion ordering guarantees the relay never promised
Hardcoding a single builder with no multiplexing or fallback: one censoring or offline builder stalls all user transactions
Ignoring the status API and resubmitting blindly from a different RPC: MetaMask-style resends leak the transaction to the public mempool before confirmation
Sharing full MEV-Share hints on latency-critical transactions while expecting maximum privacy: hint breadth trades directly against refund size and exposure
Using the private path for frontrun-immune calls (plain ETH transfers, ERC-20 approvals): pays latency and trust cost for zero protection benefit
avoid_when: The transaction calls a known frontrun-immune function (simple transfer, approval): public mempool submission is cheaper and faster
Sub-second deterministic inclusion is required: private inclusion competes per-block and may wait up to the retry window
No trust in any third-party relay or builder is acceptable: the pattern inherently delegates pre-inclusion visibility to intermediaries
The chain has no builder market or private-relay infrastructure: there is nowhere private to send the transaction
Full censorship-resistance is the goal: a censoring builder set can still delay or exclude the transaction
best_practices: Default to multiplexed (fast) mode so the transaction reaches every registered builder within one block and lands with the winning block
Never switch RPCs or resubmit from another endpoint before confirmation: parallel public submission exposes the transaction to MEV bots
Poll the Protect status API instead of Etherscan for pending private transactions; they are invisible on public explorers until included
Tune MEV-Share hints deliberately: hash-only for maximum privacy, broader hints only when chasing larger backrun refunds
Expose a cancel path that pauses relay resubmission, and stop resubmission when base-fee drift makes the transaction underpriced
Prefer exclusive submission (no side-gossip to other RPCs/builders) to qualify for gas-fee and MEV refunds
benefits: Frontrunning and sandwich protection: transactions bypass the public mempool so searcher bots never see them pre-inclusion
No fee for failed transactions: bundles are simulated and only included when they do not revert
Top-of-block priority: builder-routed transactions are placed ahead of public-mempool flow
MEV refunds: backrun value created by the transaction is partially returned to the sender via MEV-Share instead of captured entirely by searchers
Gas-fee refunds on exclusive high-priority submissions: part of the priority fee can flow back to the user
Wallet-level integration simplicity: protection is a different RPC URL, not a new signing or contract flow
component_types: Private RPC Endpoint: wallet-facing JSON-RPC ingress (e.g. rpc.flashbots.net) that validates, simulates, and forwards eth_sendRawTransaction off the gossip network
Relay / Bundle Pool: off-gossip holding area that formats transactions as bundles and resubmits them per block for up to ~25 blocks
Builder Network: competing block builders that receive private orderflow, order it, and bid built blocks into the proposer auction (MEV-Boost/PBS)
Status and Cancellation API: Protect transaction API reporting pending/simulated/included state plus a cancel request that pauses resubmission
MEV-Share Node: opt-in backrun market that shares configurable hints with searchers and redistributes captured MEV to sender, searchers, and validators
context: On Ethereum-like chains every pending transaction gossiped to the public mempool is visible to MEV searcher bots, which frontrun, sandwich, and backrun user swaps, causing slippage and failed-transaction fees. Flashbots Protect replaces gossip submission with a private orderflow path: the wallet sends signed transactions to a private RPC endpoint that forwards them directly to trusted block builders, keeping them hidden from the public mempool until they are committed inside a proposed block. Simulation before inclusion means reverting transactions never land and never cost gas.
design_principles: Pre-confirmation Privacy: orderflow stays out of the public gossip network until block inclusion, collapsing the searcher-visible window
Simulate Before Commit: every bundle is preflighted so only non-reverting transactions reach builders
Multiplex for Inclusion: share with all registered builders within one block so the transaction rides the winning block
Explicit Trust Boundary: the endpoint and each builder are named trusted parties, and per-builder sharing is user-configurable
Refund Alignment: backrun value created by user orderflow is split with the user instead of fully captured by searchers

technology_stack: Flashbots relay / MEV-Share node with hint-based privacy settings
MEV-Boost sidecar and PBS builder-relay market for block inclusion
Protect Transaction Status API (protect.flashbots.net) for pending/included tracking
tradeoffs: Trusted-intermediary risk: builders and the relay see orderflow pre-inclusion and must be trusted not to frontrun or leak it
Inclusion delay: private transactions compete per block and may wait or expire after the ~25-block retry window instead of landing immediately
Censorship exposure: a dominant or compliant builder set can delay or exclude transactions; mitigation needs builder diversity
Privacy-refund tension: broader MEV-Share hints raise refunds but widen exposure; maximum privacy minimizes refunds
Post-inclusion ordering still builder-controlled: backrunning within the builder's block remains possible by design
Fallback leakage: any parallel public-mempool submission (e.g. RPC switch before confirmation) voids the protection
use_cases: DEX swaps needing sandwich/frontrun protection at wallet submission time
Large trades that create backrun MEV the sender wants partially refunded via MEV-Share
Whitehat rescues constructed interactively as atomic bundles that must land together
High-priority-fee transactions seeking gas-fee refunds through exclusive builder submission
Wallet and dApp integrations that want MEV protection via an RPC URL change alone
